headline: Broad gains as geopolitical tensions push oil higher
deck: Equity markets climbed across the board today as Middle East friction sent crude surging, while Treasury yields edged up on growing inflation concerns.
body:
All three major indices posted solid gains this morning, with the Dow slightly outpacing peers at +0.97% while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both advanced roughly 0.85-0.87%. The broad-based rally reflects modest risk appetite despite a backdrop of escalating geopolitical turmoil. Treasury yields ticked up 12 basis points to 4.95%, suggesting markets are pricing in inflation pressures from supply-chain disruptions.

The day's primary driver remains the Iran-Saudi tension and Houthi attacks on shipping lanes and Saudi infrastructure. Oil prices surged 3% as pipeline attacks reduced supply, with the shipping sector hit particularly hard—AirBaltic has already filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy citing war-related cost pressures. Energy stocks likely benefited from the crude rally, while transportation and logistics faced headwinds.

Markets appear to be treating today's geopolitical spike as a near-term volatility event rather than a systemic threat to equities. Investors are balancing higher energy costs and supply concerns against the positive backdrop of steady economic activity, resulting in modest equity gains. The broader question for the week ahead is whether escalation continues or if tensions stabilize, which will determine whether these gains hold.
